predecessors.name: County of Holstein
predecessors.text: the County of Holstein-Rendsburg, 'elevated to a duchy by Emperor Frederick III in 1474'

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: Holstein, annexed 'by decree of December 24, 1866' and made part of the Province of Schleswig-Holstein

ledger.x: 1474: Emperor Frederick III raises Holstein to a duchy.
1474: the Duchy of Holstein is held in union with the Danish crown.
6 June 1523: the Kalmar Union ends as the Danish crown's name.
How 1523-1526 is handled: the relation is drawn as continuous and the new overlord is named from 6 June 1523.
1640: Holstein-Pinneberg falls to the royal part of the duchy.
14 January 1814: Denmark-Norway ends at the Treaty of Kiel ('Treaty of Kiel: 14 January 1814'; 'King Frederick VI had to cede the Kingdom of Norway').
14 January 1814: the Danish kingdom after Kiel holds Holstein as duke.
March 1848: Holstein rises against Denmark.
April 1851: Danish rule returns to Holstein.
24 December 1863: the German Confederation executes against the Danish king as duke.
30 October 1864: the Danish king gives up Holstein.
1864: the federal occupation ends (bridging).
30 October 1864: Holstein passes to Austria and Prussia together.
30 October 1864: the Prussian share of the joint holding (see the Austrian event of the same date).
14 August 1865: the Gastein Convention ends the joint holding; Austria's sole administration follows (next event).

14 August 1865: under the Gastein Convention Prussia leaves Holstein to Austria and takes the administration of Schleswig ('Prussia and Austria took over the administration of Schleswig and Holstein respectively').
14 August 1865: Austria takes over the administration of Holstein.
9 June 1866: Prussia invades Holstein.
23 August 1866: the Peace of Prague ends Austria's part in Holstein.
24 December 1866: the Prussian occupation becomes annexation: 'annexed both Schleswig and Holstein by decree of December 24, 1866'.
24 December 1866: Prussia annexes Holstein.

wars.name: First Schleswig War
wars.outcome: A Danish victory, 'status quo ante bellum': the Treaty of Berlin of 2 July 1850 between Prussia and Denmark, Danish victory at Idstedt on 24-25 July 1850, the rebel army disbanded on 1 April 1851, and the London Protocol of 8 May 1852 kept the duchies joined…

wars.name: Second Schleswig War
wars.outcome: Denmark lost: 'Christian IX of Denmark had to renounce both Schleswig and Holstein in the Treaty of Vienna (1864) on October 30'; Austria and Prussia administered the duchies, Holstein by Austria from 14 August 1865.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Prussia annexed Schleswig and Holstein by decree of 24 December 1866.

certainty.note: A duchy of partitioned shares (Gottorp, royal, Pinneberg) within the Elbe-Eider land; the pages give no boundary.
A member state of the German Confederation from 1815 with the Eider as its northern boundary; sharp by reading, no survey is on the page.
